title: Reds’ Hunter Greene to undergo season-ending elbow surgery for partially torn ligament
content:
WASHINGTON — Cincinnati Reds pitcher Hunter Greene will undergo season-ending elbow surgery next week on a partially torn ligament, Reds president of business operations Nick Krall said on Friday. It’s not immediately known how the procedure will affect 2027.

Krall said the exact nature of the procedure would be determined when he goes in.

“They’re going to go in there, find out what it is and go from there,” he said. “The ligament was failing. It’s going to be some sort of procedure around the ligament.”

This will be Greene’s second ligament surgery. He also had Tommy John surgery on his right elbow while in the minors in 2018.

Greene went on the 15-day injured list Wednesday, just five starts into his return from arthroscopic elbow surgery in March that involved removing bone chips.  Krall said the Reds aren’t sure if the bone chip procedure impacted the ligament, which was in good condition in the spring. Krall said Greene was sore on and off for a few weeks but didn’t bring it to anyone’s attention until recently.

“He felt like he was working through aches and pains of coming back from the bone chips,” manager Terry Francona said. “The other day I grabbed him and said, ‘Hey, I’d love for you to go out and pitch, but I wouldn’t love for you to go out and pitch and worry. I said, ‘You’re trying to throw the ball 100 miles per hour with breakoff sliders.’ I said, ‘In my opinion, it would be way easier to get you looked at instead of just hoping.’ And I’m really glad we did because he didn’t want to. I get that. He wanted to pitch.”

Greene had an MRI on Wednesday morning and went to Los Angeles for a second opinion from Dr. Neal ElAttrache, the same surgeon who did the bone chips procedure.

A 2024 All-Star and the second selection in the 2017 MLB Draft, Greene’s talent has long been considered elite. He’s a 2024 All-Star with high-level stuff, but his inability to remain healthy and on the field has overshadowed that. He’s been on the IL in each of his five seasons since his 2022 big-league debut. Last year, he was on the IL twice but had a 2.76 ERA in 19 starts with 132 strikeouts over 107 2/3 innings.
